evals.name: eval-1-mixed-stack
assertions: Flags ReadOnlyPlaylist.add() throwing (LSP / refused bequest) as reachable through PlaylistImporter + curatedPlaylists(), at P1
Flags CartSummary holding money in Double (floating point) at P1
Flags the free-shipping threshold disagreement between CartSummary.kt (50.0) and shipping.ts (3500 cents) as duplicated/diverged business rule
Flags ProfileViewModel.load() taking on networking/decoding/caching/formatting (SRP and/or bypassing the use case)
Reports the ProfileViewModel.load() responsibility problem once, not as separate SRP and layering comments on the same code
Flags the hasUnreadMessages getter's side effect (markAllAsSeen)
Flags StorageProviderFactory as speculative generality (YAGNI), or explicitly lists it as a held-back finding
Flags exportDrafts(drafts, true, false, true) boolean flag arguments, or explicitly lists it as a held-back finding
Does NOT flag the repeated arrange blocks in ProfileViewModelTests as DRY
Does NOT flag SearchHitDto / FeedItemDto as duplication
Does NOT flag the HTTPMethod switch as an OCP problem
Proposes at most 5 P3 design findings (extras noted as held back)
Findings table is ordered P1 before P2 before P3

Output opens with the 15-row ASCII outline logo banner (inverted-T visor) in a code block, with AdversaryPR v<latest version> (latest) on its middle row, where <latest version> is the Latest version line in SKILL.md
Flags that ProfileViewModel.load() never checks the HTTP response status before decoding
Every finding states a concrete failure scenario (an input or sequence of events and what goes wrong) or, for design findings, a named cost
No sarcastic, blaming, or personal language in any comment
No comment contains the words adversarial, hostile, tough, or blunt

Every comment ends with one footer line, after a blank line, of the form `Comment by <name> using Adversary ([adversarypr.com](https://adversarypr.com))`; the footer is inside each finding's `content` in findings.json
The footer's address is a markdown link to https://adversarypr.com, written `[adversarypr.com](https://adversarypr.com)`
The comments do not all open the same way (`I noticed that ...` may start some, but not all, and is never required); each gets to the point in its first sentence or two
Where only the author can know the intent, the comment asks one genuine, specific question; where the code already shows the intent, it states the problem and a way forward without a forced question

The comment text is plain: short sentences (most under 15 words, none over 25) and everyday words, at about a 4th-grade reading level, and gentle: fixes are offered as suggestions ("you could", "one way is"), never orders; code and names are left as they are
Every P1 and P2 comment contains the sentence `Please take a look at the suggested fix below, unless this was intentional.`
Every P1 and P2 comment shows the fix in a fenced code block (a language block or a ```diff block), not only in prose
No comment uses a ```suggestion block (Azure DevOps has no suggested-change feature)
